title: Senator Pete Ricketts shares updates on constituent issues and legislative actions
text:
Senator Pete Ricketts, US Senator for Nebraska | Sen. Pete Ricketts Official U.S. Senate headshot
Senator Pete Ricketts, US Senator for Nebraska | Sen. Pete Ricketts Official U.S. Senate headshot
Senator Pete Ricketts has recently highlighted a series of constituent concerns and legislative actions on his social media account.
On November 18, 2025, Senator Ricketts posted about meeting Paul in Broken Bow, Nebraska. He wrote, "Meet Paul in Broken Bow. Paul helps lead Off Broadway Apartments, a senior living community. COVID requirements made it difficult for Paul to pay his staff. Bureaucratic red tape made it difficult for Paul to receive the Employee Retention Credit. Without it, he would be forced https://t.co/1KbST7pcDn". The Employee Retention Credit was established as part of federal pandemic relief efforts but has faced criticism from small business owners who say that administrative hurdles have limited access.
Later that evening, on November 19, 2025, Senator Ricketts addressed ongoing calls for transparency regarding Jeffrey Epstein’s criminal activities. In his post he stated, "Jeffrey Epstein committed disgusting, illegal acts. I’ve long pushed for transparency and the release of the Epstein files. That’s why I supported passage tonight. I appreciate Leader Thune for passing it through the Senate as quickly as possible." Efforts to unseal documents related to Epstein's case have been widely discussed in Congress and among advocacy groups seeking greater public disclosure.
The following day, on November 19, 2025, Senator Ricketts recounted another constituent issue involving delays with FAA medical certifications: "Earlier this year, one of my constituents reached out to my office. He was frustrated with the time it takes the FAA to review medical certifications for pilots. He had waited several months for his certificate to get an upgrade.
My team was able to contact the FAA and upgrade". Delays in processing pilot medical certificates by the Federal Aviation Administration have been reported nationwide due to increased demand and resource constraints.
Senator Pete Ricketts represents Nebraska in the United States Senate after previously serving as Governor of Nebraska.
